the: used before a noun to refer to a specific or already-known thing
The cat sat quietly on the windowsill all afternoon.
seeds: small hard parts of a plant from which new plants grow
Farmers store seeds carefully so they will germinate in spring.
that: used to identify a specific thing, person, or clause already mentioned
The book that you gave me last year is still on my shelf.
wait: to stay in a place or delay action until something happens
The baker's real skill lies in knowing when to wait and when to stop.
under: in a position below something; less than
A supermarket loaf can be mixed, risen and baked in under three hours.
every: used to refer to each member of a group without exception

meadow: a field covered in grass, especially one used for hay or grazing
Wildflowers bloomed across the meadow in early summer.
lies: is positioned somewhere, or says untrue things (he/she/it)

second: coming after the first in order
The second attempt succeeded where the first had failed.
buried: covered with earth or hidden beneath a surface
Archaeologists found a buried city beneath the desert sands.
and: used to connect words, phrases, or clauses

patient: a person who is receiving medical treatment

trench: a long, narrow ditch dug in the ground

an: used before a word starting with a vowel sound to mean 'one'

old: having lived or existed for a long time; not new or young

field: an area of open land, often used for crops or animals

leave: to go away from a place, or to allow something to remain

soil: the top layer of earth in which plants grow

exposed: left uncovered or unprotected; made visible

within: inside; before a period of time has passed

few: a small number of; not many

weeks: Within weeks, algae settle on the new surface underwater.
plants: living things that grow in soil, usually with leaves and roots
She waters her plants every morning before going to work.
will: used to express the future tense
A fact heard once looks, from the inside, like a fact that will never be needed again.
appear: to become visible or to seem to be the case
Stars begin to appear in the sky shortly after sunset.
along: moving or extending in a continuous line on
Children were riding their bikes along the river path yesterday afternoon.
cut: a line, opening, or channel made by cutting into something
Wildflowers soon appeared along the cut left by the new road.
were: past tense of 'be', used for plural or 'you'

nowhere: not anywhere; in, at, or to no place
không nơi nào, không đến đâu
The lost trail seemed to lead nowhere in the thick forest.
to: expressing direction, purpose, or a recipient
The sun has set, the traffic has thinned, and yet the air refuses to cool.
be: to exist, or to have a particular state or quality

seen: The old photographs had not been seen for decades.
in: expressing location inside or within something
The keys are in the top drawer of the desk.
surrounding: Smoke from the fire drifted over the surrounding countryside for days.
grass: a common green plant with narrow leaves, often covering fields and lawns
The children played barefoot on the soft grass.
they: used to refer to people or things already mentioned, as the subject
They arrived late because of heavy traffic on the highway.
did: past tense of 'do', used to form questions and negatives or as a main verb
She did all her homework before watching television last night.
not: used to make a statement, verb, or phrase negative
The results are not as clear as we had hoped.
blow: to be moved by wind or air, or to move air forcefully
Autumn leaves blow across the yard on windy afternoons.
already: before now or before a particular time
By the time we arrived, the meeting had already started.
there: in, at, or to that place; used to show that something exists
There is a small cafe just around the corner.
waiting: the act of staying somewhere until something happens
The recipe is mostly a set of instructions about waiting in the right conditions.
surface: the outer or top layer of something
Dust had settled evenly across the wooden surface of the old table.
holds: remains true or applicable; third person singular of hold

reserve: an amount of something kept for future use
The country keeps a large reserve of rice for emergencies.
of: used to show belonging, origin, or a relationship between two things
The cover of the book was torn at the corner.
ecologists: scientists who study the relationships between living things and their environment
Ecologists are tracking how the forest recovers after the fire.
call: to name or describe something in a particular way
Scientists call this rare weather pattern a polar vortex.
seed: the small part of a plant from which a new plant grows
She planted the seed in early spring and watched it sprout.
bank: a stored supply of something, or a financial institution

plant: to put a seed or young plant in the ground to grow

has: has; present tense of have, third person singular

grown: having developed or increased over time
The ivy has grown all the way up to the roof this summer.
nearby: not far away; close at hand
We found a nearby café that served excellent coffee.
for: intended to belong to, or be given to, someone or something
She bought a small gift for her best friend.
years: Somebody must own the roof and repaint it every few years.
been: past participle of be, used to show a completed state or experience
They have been friends since primary school.
dropping: Autumn leaves keep dropping onto the quiet garden path.
into: moving towards the inside of something
She walked into the room and switched on the light.
it: used to refer to a thing, animal, or situation already mentioned

only: and no one or nothing more besides; just

fraction: a small part or amount of something

those: used to refer to people or things further away or already mentioned
Those houses on the hill were built a century ago.
ever: Nobody can write down rules that nobody ever actually knew.
germinate: to begin to grow, as a seed does
The seeds germinate within a week of watering.
year: Everyone agrees the device runs for only a handful of minutes a year.
fall: a decrease in amount, level, or value
The report records a steady fall in river fish populations.
rest: the part of something that remains, or a period of relaxation
phần còn lại, sự nghỉ ngơi
After a short rest, they continued walking up the hill.
go: to move or travel from one place to another
We should go before the traffic gets worse.
quiet: making little or no noise; calm
The library is usually quiet enough for deep concentration.
going: The situation is going from bad to worse.
is: present tense (he/she/it) of the verb be
The library is open until nine o'clock every evening.
same: They wore the same colour shirts to the reunion.
as: used to compare, or to mean 'while' or 'because'
As the sun set, the temperature dropped quickly.
dying: in the process of death, or gradually ending
The fire was slowly dying as the last logs burned out.
dormant: temporarily inactive but capable of becoming active again
ở trạng thái ngủ (không hoạt động)
The volcano had been dormant for over two hundred years.
keeps: continues to have, hold, or maintain something (he/she/it)
Regular exercise keeps the body strong and flexible.
its: belonging to a thing, animal, or situation already mentioned
The cat licked its paw before curling up to sleep.
machinery: machines collectively, or the working parts of a system
Heavy machinery was brought in to clear the collapsed building.
intact: complete and not damaged or changed
The ancient vase survived the earthquake completely intact.
but: used to introduce something contrasting with what has just been said
She wanted to stay longer, but the last train was leaving soon.
slows: Heavy rain always slows the traffic on this road.
almost: very nearly but not completely or entirely
She almost missed the last train home after the concert ended.
stop: to come to an end or cause something to end
The bus will stop right outside the school gate.
depending: Prices vary depending on the season and the size of the room.
on: positioned at or touching the surface of something
She placed the keys on the table by the door.
species: a group of living things that can breed together and share characteristics
Scientists discovered a new species of frog in the rainforest.
may: The meeting may be postponed if too few people attend.
hold: keep or retain something, such as water or an object
These containers hold enough water for a week.
state: the particular condition that someone or something is in
The old car was in a terrible state after the crash.
season: one of the main periods of the year, or a period of a particular activity
Mango season brings extra income to farmers each year.
decade: The city's population has doubled over the past decade.
or: used to link alternatives or possibilities
Would you like tea or coffee with your breakfast?
very: used to make an adjective or adverb stronger
The soup tasted very good after such a cold walk.
much: to a great extent or degree
The new design does not cost much more than the old one.
longer: for a greater length of time
Fresh bread stays soft for longer if wrapped properly.
some: an unspecified amount or number of something
Could you buy some bread on your way home?
documented: recorded in written or official form
The unusual weather pattern was carefully documented by researchers.
cases: plural of case; instances or examples of a situation
Hospitals reported a sharp rise in flu cases this winter.
run: to move quickly, or to continue moving under its own momentum
The car will run for a while even after the engine dies.
well: in a good or satisfactory way
The bicycle still balanced perfectly well even with the gyroscopic effect cancelled out.
over: during the whole of a period of time; more than
Prices have risen steadily over the past five years.
century: a period of one hundred years
The tradition has been passed down for more than a century.
what: used to ask for information about something
The reason lies in what cities are actually made of.
breaks: separates into pieces, or stops working, suddenly
A sudden noise usually breaks the silence of the empty hall.
signal: an event or sound that gives a message or triggers an action
The referee's whistle is the signal for the game to begin.
signals: events or sounds that give messages or trigger actions
The brain constantly receives signals from nerves throughout the body.
are: present tense form of 'to be' used with you, we, they
They are planning to visit their grandparents next weekend.
surprisingly: in a way that is unexpected
The exam was surprisingly easy compared to last year's version.
specific: Please give me a specific date for the meeting.
many: Many residents still remember the flood of that year.
trigger: an event or factor that causes something to happen
For many species the trigger is light.
light: the natural energy that makes things visible
Soft light filled the room through the open curtains.
darkness: the state of having little or no light
The power cut left the entire street in darkness for hours.
stays: continues to be in a place or condition
The lake stays frozen well into early spring.
asleep: The baby finally fell asleep after being rocked for an hour.
one: Only one seat was left when we arrived at the theatre.
turned: past tense of turn; changed direction or became something different
Both guesses turned out to be backwards.
up: towards a higher place or position
Neighbourhoods with few trees and little open space heat up fastest.
by: indicating the agent, method, or proximity of something
The letter was written by hand and delivered by courier.
plough: a farming tool used to turn over soil before planting
The old plough is now kept as a decoration on the farm.
does: performs an action, or auxiliary form used in questions and negatives
She does her best to help everyone around her.
others: other people or things not already mentioned
Some students finished early, while others needed the full hour.
swing: a movement back and forth or a change between states
There was a sudden swing in public opinion after the debate.
temperature: a measure of how hot or cold something is
The nurse checked the patient's temperature before the appointment began.
between: in the space or time separating two things
The old road runs between two small villages in the valley.
day: a period of twenty-four hours, or the time when it is light
She spent the whole day preparing for the interview.
night: the period of darkness between sunset and sunrise
The city looked completely different lit up at night.
which: used to ask about or refer to a specific choice
It is one of the clearest ways in which a city changes its weather.
happens: takes place; occurs, third person singular
It happens more often than people realise during exam season.
near: at a short distance from a place, time or state
They built their house near a small, quiet lake.
heat: the quality of being hot; thermal energy
The heat from the oven made the whole kitchen warm.
from: indicating the point where something starts or originates
The letter came from a friend living overseas.
fire: the flame, light and heat produced by burning
They gathered around the fire to keep warm at night.
smoke: the grey or black cloud produced by something burning
Thick smoke rose from the chimney on the cold morning.
each: every one of two or more things, considered separately
Each student received a copy of the new textbook.
means: A nod usually means agreement in most cultures.
thing: an object, idea, or matter not named specifically
There's one thing I still don't understand about the plan.
different: not the same as another or each other
Every student in the class has a different learning style.
words: It has no words for kitchen tools or playground arguments any more.
ground: the solid surface of the earth
Leaves covered the ground after the autumn winds.
above: in or to a higher position than something else
A hawk circled slowly above the quiet valley.
you: used to refer to the person being spoken to
The method also feels worse while you are doing it.
disturbed: The soil was disturbed when workers dug the new foundation.
shading: The awning is useful for shading the porch in summer.
gone: departed, disappeared, or no longer present
By the time we arrived, the bus was already gone.
cannot: used to say that something is not possible or not allowed
Visitors cannot enter the site without prior written permission.
see: to perceive something with the eyes
From the hilltop you can see the whole valley below.
gap: a difference or space between two things
The gap between rich and poor neighbourhoods keeps growing.
canopy: the uppermost spreading layer of branches and leaves in a forest
Sunlight barely reaches the forest floor beneath the thick canopy.
can: used to express ability or possibility
Anyone with an internet connection can join the online course.
detect: to discover or notice the presence of something
The new sensor can detect even the smallest gas leak.
conditions: circumstances that affect how something happens
Farmers watch weather conditions closely before planting their crops.
produces: The volcano regularly produces small clouds of ash and steam.
this: used to refer to a specific thing nearby or just mentioned
This is the best coffee I have had in years.
consequences: results or effects of actions or conditions
Ignoring the warning signs had serious consequences for the whole team.
anyone: Anyone interested in the workshop should sign up before Friday.
trying: present participle of try; making an attempt to do something
Closing the book and trying to write the same content from memory feels far worse but works far better.
restore: to bring something back to its former condition
Volunteers worked to restore the damaged wetland habitat.
damaged: harmed or injured in a way that reduces value or usefulness
The damaged bridge remained closed to traffic for several months.
habitat: the natural home of an animal or plant
Logging destroyed much of the bird's original habitat.
sometimes: on some occasions but not always
Sometimes she walks to work instead of driving.
replanting: the act of planting again after clearance or loss
Replanting the burned forest will take several decades.
unnecessary: not needed; more than is required
Sometimes replanting is unnecessary: clear the ground, wait, and the old community returns.
clear: easy to understand, see, or perceive; free from confusion
The instructions were clear enough for a beginner to follow.
community: a group of people living in the same place or sharing something
The whole community gathered to celebrate the festival in the town square.
returns: The bird returns to the same nest every spring.
underneath: in a position below something else
That turn moves the wheels back underneath the falling weight, and the bicycle straightens.
hopeless: having no hope of success or improvement
The rescue attempt seemed hopeless after the storm hit.
because: They cancelled the picnic because it started to rain.
emptied: made empty by removing everything from something
The reservoir was emptied for repairs during the dry season.
decades: The old bridge has stood for decades without major repairs.
ploughing: the act of turning over soil with a plough
Ploughing in autumn helps prepare the soil for spring planting.
nothing: There was nothing left in the fridge by Friday evening.
left: remaining after others have gone or been used
Only a few seats were left by the time we arrived.
wake: to stop sleeping, or to cause someone to stop sleeping
They still go to sleep and wake at regular times each day.
depth: the distance from the top or surface to the bottom
The pool's depth increases gradually from the shallow end.
matters: In a job interview, first impressions really matter.
age: the length of time a person or thing has existed
Her grandfather still plays chess sharply despite his age.
woken: Seeds near the surface are woken by every passing disturbance.
passing: lasting only a short time; happening while moving by
He gave only a passing glance at the newspaper headlines.
disturbance: an interruption of a peaceful or normal condition
Neighbours complained about the disturbance caused by the late-night party.
two: Two things mark it as worth keeping.
deeper: Miners had to dig deeper to reach the coal seam.
insulated: protected from heat, cold, or, figuratively, from outside influence
The old house was poorly insulated, so it felt cold in winter.
swings: movements back and forth or changes between states
Doctors watched for mood swings during the first weeks of treatment.
germination: the process by which a seed begins to grow
Warm soil speeds up the germination of most seeds.
turning: moving or rotating in a circular direction
An effect anyone can feel by holding a turning wheel by its axle.
brings: carries or takes something to a place
Spring always brings warmer weather and blooming flowers to the region.
deep: positioned far down from the surface
Tree roots often grow deep into the soil to find water.
ones: particular items or people already mentioned or understood
The smaller phones sell better than the larger ones this year.
all: the whole quantity or extent of something
She spent all summer preparing for the entrance exam.
at: used to show a specific place, time or point
We agreed to meet at the station at six o'clock.
once: immediately, without delay (used in the phrase 'at once')
The fire alarm made everyone leave the building at once.
why: Why does the air above a city stay warm long after sunset?
ploughed: turned over soil using a plough (past tense)
The farmer ploughed the field before the rainy season began.
after: following in time or place; later than
The shop stays open late after the holiday season begins.
long: having a great length or duration
It was a long journey across three different countries.
neglect: failure to give proper care or attention to something
Years of neglect left the old building in poor condition.
produce: This factory can produce thousands of bicycles every single month.
flush: a sudden abundant growth or supply of something
Spring rain brings a flush of new grass to the hillside.
nobody: not a single person; no one
Nobody expected the small team to win the championship.
living: She is one of the few living witnesses to that event.
memory: the ability to store and recall information
His memory for names and faces has always been impressive.
so: used to show the result or consequence of something
It started raining, so we decided to stay indoors.
first: coming before all others in order or time
She was the first person to arrive at the meeting.

n
a sentence asked to get information or express doubt
câu hỏi, vấn đề

query
inquiry
issue
restoration: the act of returning something to its former condition

team: a group of people who work or play together

asks: puts a question to someone or requests something

down: toward a lower position or level

answered: gave a response to a question or problem

taking: getting hold of, removing, or carrying something
